notes.inflation: Inflation is the Census and Statistics Department's Composite Consumer Price Index as the IMF republishes it. The interest rate is the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's base rate, shown from October 1998, when it was introduced. Because the Hong Kong dollar is linked to the US dollar, the base rate moves with the US federal funds rate.
notes.labour: GDP is quarterly, from the Census and Statistics Department: current prices, and chained (2024) dollars for real GDP. Growth on the previous quarter is seasonally adjusted; the levels are not. Unemployment is the International Labour Organization's modelled annual estimate, published by the World Bank.
notes.trade: Goods trade is Hong Kong's monthly data as the IMF republishes it, in US dollars, converted to Hong Kong dollars at each month's average exchange rate from the Bank for International Settlements. Most of Hong Kong's exports are re-exports of goods made elsewhere. Exports are valued free on board, imports including cost, insurance and freight.
notes.public: Debt and the budget balance are the IMF World Economic Outlook's general government figures, actual years only, so estimates and projections never appear as data.
notes.markets: The exchange rate is the Federal Reserve's daily rate. The Hong Kong dollar has been linked to the US dollar since October 1983 and held between 7.75 and 7.85 per US dollar since 2005, so it barely moves, and Dollarise changes the level of a series but not its shape. There is no 10-year government bond yield or business confidence index on this page.
